conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: EXCEPTION-OBJECT
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR1: "EXCEPTION-OBJECT references the current exception object. If an exception object is not associated with the current exception, EXCEPTION-OBJECT is set to null." (cite.py --check 8.4.3.6.4 OK). Both halves verified. Object half: SetObject (RAISE identifier-1, §14.9.29.4 GR2 --check OK; GOBACK/EXIT RAISING staging) stores the object; probe p1.cob RAISE E then `IF EXCEPTION-OBJECT = E` answers DECL-SAME inside the USE AFTER EXCEPTION OBJECT declarative and AFTER-SAME after return (identity, not merely non-null). Null half: no exception -> null (golden pb922 SR2-NULL=YES); Set (every named raise, §14.6.13.1.1 'the predefined object reference EXCEPTION-OBJECT is set to null' --check OK; SetIo delegates to Set) nulls it - probe: RAISE E then an EC-SIZE raise under >>TURN EC-SIZE CHECKING ON / ON SIZE ERROR answers NAMED-NULL; Clear (SET LAST EXCEPTION TO OFF, §14.9.39.4 GR28 --check OK) nulls it - probe OFF-NULL. Same output at --std 2002/2014/2023. Test-ref left empty: pb922_exception_object_reference pins only the no-exception null arm and oo_ec_raise_object only asserts NOT = NULL (no spec derivation header, no identity check); no existing spec-derived test pins identity with the raised object or the null-after-named-raise arm - test-needed.
rows.rule-text: EXCEPTION-OBJECT references the current exception object. If an exception object is not associated with the current exception, EXCEPTION-OBJECT is set to null.

rows.subject: EXCEPTION-OBJECT
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR2: "There is one instance of EXCEPTION-OBJECT in a run unit." (cite.py --check 8.4.3.6.4 OK). The register is not storage in any program: every read renders to ExceptionState.ExceptionObject, a facade over RunUnit.Current.Exceptions - one ExceptionEngine owned by the run unit (AsyncLocal RunUnit, one per run unit, concurrently-hosted run units each get their own). Probe p1.cob: main RAISEs object E, then CALLs a separately compiled program EXOBJS1 (own PROGRAM-ID, same run unit) which reads EXCEPTION-OBJECT and answers SUB-SHARED (not null) at 2002/2014/2023. Test-ref empty: golden pb922's GR2-ONE=SAME compares two null reads inside one program, which cannot distinguish one instance from per-program instances; a cross-program witness with a non-null object is test-needed. [code-location note: (static facade E => RunUnit.Current.Exceptions); code-location note: (ExceptionObjectRegister, one shared per program model, ~l.298-314)]
rows.rule-text: There is one instance of EXCEPTION-OBJECT in a run unit.

rows.subject: EXIT and GOBACK statements (execution continuation in a non-COBOL runtime element)
rows.adjudicator-notes: §14.9.18.4 GR1 a) (cite.py --check 14.9.18.4 'execution continues in the activating element in an implementor-defined fashion' -> OK §14.9.18.4 1) a)); §14.9.14.4 GR3 routes EXIT PROGRAM to §14.9.18 (read). Condition met: a .NET host can activate a program. Probe (built outside the repo): /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s2/probe/gb/sub2.cob compiled to sub.dll (GOBACK, then EXIT PROGRAM variant, at 2023 and EXIT PROGRAM at 85/2002), host /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s2/probe/gbhost/Program.cs loads it by reflection, invokes __CobolModule.Register, ProgramRegistry.CallProgram('SUBP','',[],null) twice -> 'HOST BEFORE / IN SUBP / HOST RESUMED / IN SUBP / HOST RESUMED 2', exit 0, 'NOT REACHED' never printed. Generated sub.g.cs: internal sealed _PRG_SUBP.__Activate 'try { __Dispatch } catch (ProgramReturn) { }', public static __CobolModule.Register -> ProgramRegistry.Register. The row corrects §3 prose's 'invokes a generated program class directly' (the class is internal; the entry is ProgramRegistry.CallProgram). RETURNING / RAISING halves are delegated to the §3 prose (read, not re-probed). No spec-derived test drives a non-COBOL activator (Pinned by '-'). Owning note: PB1534.
rows.rule-text: EXIT and GOBACK statements (execution continuation in a non-COBOL runtime element). This item is conditionally required, because it is conditioned upon support for calling from non-COBOL programs. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (14.9.18, GOBACK statement, General rule 3)

rows.subject: End markers
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py: OK §10.7.4 '1) An end marker indicates the end of the specified source unit.' The grammar closes a unit at its end marker: nestedProgram requires endProgramHeader, and classDefinition, factory, object, method and interface each end in their own END. p4 shows a unit contained in another and closed by END PROGRAM running as the nested program. In a program that breaks SR3 (p3), the marker closes the innermost open unit whatever name it gives. That is the SR3 under-reject and does not change what a conforming program means. No spec-derived test covers this directly. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 1985+ (program); 2002+ (OO/function units)
rows.rule-text: An end marker indicates the end of the specified source unit.

rows.subject: Entry-name clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: "Data-name-1 shall not be qualified or subscripted." (cite.py --check 13.18.20.3 OK, rule 1). dataName is a single cobolWord/FILLER token with no qualifier or subscript alternative, so the declaration slot cannot carry either: probe/entry-name-clause/p4.cob `05 A OF G PIC X(3).` -> COBOL0001 near 'OF'; p5.cob `05 A(1) PIC X(3).` -> COBOL0001 near '('. Report group name (cobolWord) likewise. Rejection is a generic parse error, not a named diagnostic — acceptable for a syntax rule. No spec-derived negative test pins it. || Editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause's own text; Annex E records no change to the entry-name clause)
rows.rule-text: Data-name-1 shall not be qualified or subscripted.

rows.subject: Environment division structure
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule §12.2.1: 'ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.' (both words underlined, period required) followed by '[ configuration-section ]' then '[ input-output-section ]' -- both optional, in that order. Grammar environmentDivision = ENVIRONMENT DIVISION DOT configurationSection? inputOutputSection? matches exactly (no binder/validation pass narrows it; ClosedFormatPass line 132 only names the node). Probed with pinned cobol.exe at --std 85/2002/2014/2023: empty division, CONFIGURATION only, INPUT-OUTPUT only, both in order, empty section headers alone -> all compile and run correctly; INPUT-OUTPUT before CONFIGURATION -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'CONFIGURATION' (correct rejection, order is fixed by the format); header without period -> COBOL0307 (correct). cite.py --check 12.2.1 '[ configuration-section ]' -> OK; '[ input-output-section ]' -> OK. No spec-derived test targets this format (order rejection has no negative golden) -> test-ref empty = test-needed. Probes: out/probe/env-div/{A,B,C,D,E,G,H,N}.cob. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §12.2.1 format carries no edition gating; unchanged across editions)]

rows.subject: Exception condition handling
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule text: cite.py --check 14.6.13.2 'the sending and receiving items in a MOVE statement are defined with the same standard floating-point usage specification, with the exception of endianness' -> OK §14.6.13.2 3). Four exemptions: class condition, sign condition, same-usage MOVE (endianness aside), VALIDATE. MEASURED (probe out/probe/ecinc/r3.cob, FLOAT-BINARY-64 HIGH-ORDER-LEFT leaf planted with NaN bytes X"7FF8000000000000" via REDEFINES, >>TURN EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE CHECKING ON, at 2023 and 2014): DISPLAY F, ADD 1 TO F, MOVE F TO S9(5), IF F > 0, MOVE F TO FLOAT-BINARY-32, MOVE F TO FLOAT-LONG (a different usage), COMPUTE N = F * 0 with +Inf -> all RAISED; IF F POSITIVE (sign) exempt; IF F IS FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER (class) exempt, true; MOVE F TO FLOAT-BINARY-64 HIGH-ORDER-LEFT (same usage) and MOVE F TO FLOAT-BINARY-64 HIGH-ORDER-RIGHT (same usage, other endianness) exempt, and both receivers then test NaN (verbatim transfer). SendingRefRules.FloatChecked is the four-entry exclusion list. FLOAT-DECIMAL-16/34 are refused at compile time (COBOLNET1564, Annex A.3 item 19 processor-dependent, documented) so that half is unreachable by any accepted program; VALIDATE is A.4.14 Not claimed (PB283), its exemption vacuous. CONFORMANCE.md's documented extension of the raise to every float usage (COMP-1/COMP-2/FLOAT-SHORT/LONG) is implementor latitude outside this rule. No spec-derived golden covers a STANDARD float usage: conformance:2023/ec_data_not_finite uses COMP-2/COMP-1 (the extension), so test-ref is left empty (test-needed). [code-location note: (FloatSending chokepoints); code-location note: (FloatDisplay/FloatSending); code-location note: (sign-condition exemption); code-location note: (ambient EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE gate)] || editions as adjudicated: 2014, 2023 (standard floating-point usages FLOAT-BINARY-32/64/128 and FLOAT-DECIMAL-16/34 are 2014 introductions)
rows.rule-text: When a sending operand is described with a standard floating-point usage, and the content of the sending operand would evaluate to true in an infinity class condition or to true in a FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER class condition, the EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE exception condition is set to exist, except in the following circumstances: — a sending item is referenced in a class condition, or — a sending item is referenced in a sign condition, or — the sending and receiving items in a MOVE statement are defined with the same standard floating-point usage specification, with the exception of endianness, or — a sending item is processed in a VALIDATE statement.

rows.subject: Exception conditions
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: §14.6.13.1.2 2) (cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.2 "Any directly or indirectly activated runtime element terminates the run unit" -> OK 2)). A run-unit termination inside a CALLed element unwinds as the runtime's stop signal through __RunUse's try/finally, so no -1 ('completed normally') is ever returned and no continuation after the raising statement happens. Probe n5 (out/probe/exc-normal): RAISE EC-USER-X (checked) -> USE AFTER EC declarative CALLs EXN5B which executes STOP RUN -> output 'DECL-START / B-STOPS', exit 0; neither DECL-END nor AFTER-RAISE is displayed. No existing spec-derived test found that activates a terminating element from within a declarative (test-needed). || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (EC model introduced by ISO 2002)
rows.rule-text: Any directly or indirectly activated runtime element terminates the run unit.

rows.subject: Exception conditions
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: §14.6.13.1.4 4) (cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.4 "Execution of the statement continues as specified in the rules for that statement" -> OK 4)). With checking enabled and no phrase / WHEN / USE applying, a nonfatal condition continues per the statement's rules: EmitRaise (nonfatal: no throw after a -3 dispatch), EmitOverflow (no throw), __IoCheckEc (successful arm returns -1; nonfatal unsuccessful families fall through without the fatal throw). Probe out/probe/exc-nonfatal/g4: >>TURN EC-I-O-WARNING ON, no handler, indexed WRITE yielding '02' with NOT INVALID KEY -> 'NOTINV2 02 / AFTER 02' (the WRITE's own §9.1.14 successful-completion rule applies), exit 0. No existing test asserts the enabled-no-handler continuation specifically (test-needed). || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (EC model introduced by ISO 2002)
rows.rule-text: Execution of the statement continues as specified in the rules for that statement.
